claims.text: Under simultaneous wear and corrosion, HEAs resist degradation by rapidly forming a mechanically robust, self-healing oxide film on the worn surface.
The protective film forms through selective oxidation of high-oxygen-affinity elements such as Cr and Mn.
Cr and Mn segregate to mechanically activated surface sites.
The oxide film hardens the worn surface.
The oxide film impedes corrosive dissolution.
The proposed test material is an equiatomic or near-equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni HEA with a fine-grained, chemically homogeneous microstructure and no preformed oxide film.
Simultaneous sliding wear in aerated 3.5 wt% NaCl will produce a thin, adherent, self-healing oxide film enriched mainly in Cr and Mn oxides.
Mechanical wear continuously removes the alloy's outermost layers and exposes fresh surfaces.
Freshly exposed surfaces rapidly oxidize through selective oxidation of elements having high oxygen affinity.
High configurational entropy promotes a uniform distribution of elements in the alloy.
High configurational entropy enables localized elemental segregation under mechanical stress.
Selective oxidation and stress-assisted segregation rapidly re-establish a protective passivating film in the worn region.
Re-establishment of the oxide film reduces subsequent mechanically driven material loss.
Re-establishment of the oxide film reduces active corrosion attack.
Relative to a mechanically matched, less compositionally complex baseline, the HEA will have significantly lower wear-volume loss and wear-track depth during tribocorrosion.
Relative to the baseline, the HEA will have significantly lower corrosion-pit density during tribocorrosion.
Post-test microscopy and spectroscopy will reveal a more continuous, adherent, and uniform oxide film on the HEA than on the baseline.
The proposed resistance enhancement requires simultaneous mechanical wear, corrosive exposure, and sufficient oxygen for oxide formation.
Under pure wear, pure corrosion, or oxygen-deficient conditions, the self-healing-film synergy and predicted resistance enhancement will not occur.
Film-formation kinetics and film stability depend on load, electrolyte conditions, local chemistry, and mechanical strain.
